title: Propagation processes on (hyper)graphs: where zero forcing and burning meet
summary: The burning and forcing processes are both instances of propagation processes on graphs that are commonly used to model real-world spreading phenomena. The contribution of this paper is two-fold. We first establish a connection between these two propagation processes via hypergraphs. We do so by showing a sharp upper bound on the zero forcing number of the incidence graph of a hypergraph in terms of the lazy burning number of the hypergraph, which builds up on and improves a result by Bonato, Jones, Marbach, Mishura and Zhang (Theor.
